# Paths — Unified Design Guide

**Version 1.3 · July 2026 · Source of truth for Paths UI**

This document defines the default design language for Paths across iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Widgets, and the planned Paths Web. It supersedes the legacy `ColorStyle` palette and earlier design drafts. Reuse the tokens and components below for recurring UI decisions. Platform-native behavior, specialized visualizations, and small optical corrections may use documented exceptions when the default would reduce clarity or quality.

---

## 1. Design character

Paths is a **quiet Bauhaus instrument for personal discipline**. The look is:

- **Monochrome-first.** The interface is ink on paper. Structure comes primarily from typography, spacing, alignment, and tonal grouping rather than decorative color.
- **Drawn, not boxed in.** Surfaces are flat and geometry is crisp, but borders are used only when they communicate focus, selection, or a boundary that would otherwise be unclear. Shadows are whispers, never glows.
- **One geometry.** Circles, rounded rectangles, and straight lines. No arbitrary blobs, decorative gradients on ordinary controls, or glassmorphism on new surfaces. Artwork, avatars, calendar backgrounds, and specialized visualizations may use gradients when they are intrinsic to the visual rather than surface decoration.
- **Color is information.** The four accents communicate state or reserved identity (success, action-warmth, energy/warning, info/calm, Arete). If removing a color loses no meaning, the color must not be there.
- **Calm motion.** Things settle; they never bounce for fun.

---

## 2. Color

### 2.1 The palette (final — replaces both `PathsPalette` drafts and legacy `ColorStyle`)

Core neutrals (the interface):

| Token | Light | Dark | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ink` | `#1E1C1D` | `#F2F0ED` | Primary text, outlines, icons, filled buttons |
| `ink-60` | `#1E1C1D` @ 60% | `#F2F0ED` @ 60% | Secondary text |
| `ink-40` | `#1E1C1D` @ 40% | `#F2F0ED` @ 40% | Muted text, disabled labels |
| `paper` | `#FFFFFF` | `#1C1A19` | App background, card surface |
| `paper-raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#282523` | Elevated and floating surfaces (dark mode only differs) |
| `mist` | `#E9EAE6` | `#383432` | Subtle fills: chips, input backgrounds, dividers-strong |
| `mist-40` | `#E9EAE6` @ 40% | `#383432` @ 40% | Subtle backgrounds, hairline dividers |

Accents (semantic use only — never decoration, never buttons, never headings):

| Token | Light | Dark | Meaning — the ONLY permitted uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sage` | `#87A56E` | `#9DB886` | Success and completion marks, streak kept, "done" states |
| `clay` | `#CE8B6C` | `#DBA184` | Warmth/destructive-soft: time marks, gentle-alert icons, delete confirmations |
| `ochre` | `#EECD84` | `#E8C87E` | Energy marks: warnings, streak-at-risk, in-progress highlights |
| `fjord` | `#639A88` | `#7FB0A0` | Info/calm marks: Arete (AI) identity and informational indicators |

> These are evolved from the current `PathsPalette` (`8aa870`, `d09075`, `f0d090`, `6aa090`): each nudged ~4% deeper and harmonized in oklch so all four sit at similar lightness/chroma. Migrate old values when the affected surface is touched and visually verified.

**Deleted:** the entire legacy `ColorStyle` set (`8F86A8`, `D59A73`, `CF7873`, `6F8FB3`, `8EA67C`, `4B4744`, `DCC885`, `78A39E`) and the stray `#EE9191` time-label pink → use `clay`. The Arete message-color picker set (`2F6FED`, etc.) may remain as a user-choice feature but defaults to `ink`.

### 2.2 Usage rules

1. `Color(hex:)` literals are forbidden in feature views. Only tokens.
2. Accents are used at 100% for small marks (dots, checks, short rules, icon tints) and at 20% opacity for area fills (banners, tinted chips). Never fill a large region with a 100% accent.
3. Never place two different accents in the same component. One semantic message = one color.
4. Text is `ink`/`ink-60`/`ink-40` or `paper` on an ink fill. Do not use the soft accents for small text on `paper`; they do not provide enough contrast. Put the accent in an adjacent dot, icon, check, or rule and keep the label in `ink`. Color must not be the only indication of state.
5. Progress visualizations (sphere, paths, charts): monochrome structure + **one** accent (`sage`) marking current/completed progress.
6. Dark mode is the same drawing on dark paper: outlines and text flip to `ink`(dark) — do not introduce new colors, glows, or elevation tints beyond `paper-raised`.

---

## 3. Typography

**One family: Jost.** The Bauhaus TTFs are retired — remove `Bauhaus-*.ttf` and the `titleBauhaus`/`displayBauhaus` names (they already render Jost). Weights available: Regular (400), Medium (500), SemiBold (600), Bold (700), Italic.

### 3.1 Type scale (iPhone, default Dynamic Type)

| Token | Weight / size / line-height | Case & tracking | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | Bold 34 / 40 | Sentence case, tracking −0.5 | Screen heroes: level-up card, onboarding moments. Max one per screen |
| `title` | SemiBold 24 / 30 | Sentence case | Screen titles, prominent overlay titles |
| `heading` | SemiBold 20 / 26 | Sentence case | Section headers, card titles |
| `subheading` | Medium 17 / 24 | Sentence case | Sub-sections, list-group headers, prominent rows |
| `body` | Regular 16 / 24 | Sentence case | Default text everywhere |
| `body-strong` | SemiBold 16 / 24 | — | Emphasis inside body, button labels, names |
| `meta` | Regular 15 / 20 | — | Timestamps, feed metadata |
| `caption` | Regular 13 / 18 | — | Captions, helper text, badge labels |
| `overline` | Medium 11 / 14 | UPPERCASE, tracking +1.2 | Tiny category labels above cards/sections |

Rules:
- Every text style scales with Dynamic Type (`relativeTo:` anchors: display→largeTitle, title→title, heading→title3, subheading→headline, body→callout, meta→subheadline, caption→footnote, overline→caption2).
- Do not use `.font(.system(...))` for app-authored text. App-authored text is Jost via tokens; platform-owned controls and SF Symbol sizing may use their native APIs.
- Numbers in stats/timers use Jost Medium with monospaced digits (`.monospacedDigit()`).
- Special cases keep their existing sizes as tokens: sign-up question = SemiBold 26, sign-up input = Regular 22.
- iPad regular-width: `display` 40, `title` 28, `heading` 22; body sizes unchanged — win space with layout, not bigger body text.
- Watch: `heading` 18 SemiBold, `body` 15, `caption` 12; system rendering constraints permitting, Jost everywhere.
- Web: begin with the same numeric scale in px, including body 16 px and the line-heights above, then verify optical size and platform rendering rather than assuming exact physical equivalence with iOS points.

### 3.2 Hierarchy formula

A screen has at most one `display` or `title`, followed by `heading` for major sections, `subheading` for local groups, and `body`/`meta`/`caption` for content. Do not place multiple title-sized labels in competition. Establish hierarchy with type, spacing, and alignment before introducing a container.

---

## 4. Layout and surfaces

### 4.1 Spacing — 4 pt grid

`xs 4 · sm 8 · md 12 · lg 16 · xl 24 · xxl 32 · xxxl 48`

- Screen horizontal margin: **16** (iPhone), **24** (sign-up flow and iPad).
- Card internal padding: **16**. Chip padding: 12 horizontal / 8 vertical.
- Vertical rhythm: 24 between sections, 12 between cards in a list, 8 between related rows.
- Use tokens for recurring layout and shared components. A one-off optical or geometry correction is allowed when a grid value looks wrong; keep it local, document why it exists, and promote it to a token only if it repeats.

### 4.2 Radius

`sm 8 · md 16 · lg 24 · full 999`

- Cards, buttons, inputs: `md` (16), continuous corners.
- Chips/small controls & input fields inside cards: `sm` (8).
- Large floating surfaces and prominent controls: `lg` (24).
- Circular controls and avatars: `full`.
- Keep the outer geometry of a component consistent. Nested controls and intentionally asymmetric shapes, such as chat bubbles, may use a smaller radius. Use raw values only for specialized geometry or a documented optical correction; recurring radii become tokens.

### 4.3 Borders and strokes

- **No border is the default.** Do not add a border solely to make a surface conform to the design system.
- **Quiet edge: 1 pt `mist`.** Use only when a divider or boundary is necessary for comprehension.
- **Emphasis stroke: 2 pt `ink`.** Reserve for keyboard focus, a selected state that cannot be shown clearly with fill, or an intentionally graphic hero element.
- **State stroke: 2 pt accent.** Allowed for errors or another state requiring immediate emphasis; pair it with an icon or text so color is not the only signal.
- Illustration, chart, Watch, and 3D geometry may adjust stroke width for legibility at their rendered size. These widths are not general UI-border tokens.
- Avoid nested outlines. If a parent already establishes a boundary, its children should normally use spacing or a tonal fill.

### 4.4 Elevation

Most in-flow content uses no shadow. Shadows lift a card only when it needs separation from the surrounding surface, and lift interactive or floating elements when elevation communicates behavior. Use these shared shadows:

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `shadow-card` | black 6% · radius 8 · y 2 | Cards that need separation from the background |
| `shadow-button` | black 12% · radius 2 · y 1 | Filled buttons |
| `shadow-float` | black 15% · radius 8 · y 4 | Popovers and floating buttons |

Do not combine a strong outline and a shadow on the same ordinary surface. Dark mode relies first on `paper-raised` and tonal separation; do not automatically double shadow opacity and never add light glows. Glass/`ultraThinMaterial` styling is deprecated for ordinary content cards; migrate to a flat tokenized surface without introducing a new border. The subtle card-grain shader may remain, intensity ≤ 0.35, on hero cards only.

---

## 5. Components

All components use tokens above. If a style chain appears twice, it must be a shared ViewModifier/ButtonStyle (or a web component/class).

### 5.1 Buttons

| Variant | Recipe |
|---|---|
| **Primary** | Fill `ink`, label `paper` body-strong, height 48 (min touch 44), radius `md`, `shadow-button`. Pressed: 88% opacity + scale 0.985. Disabled: `mist` fill, `ink-40` label, no shadow |
| **Secondary** | `mist-40` fill, no outline, `ink` label. Same geometry as primary. A text-button treatment is preferred for low-priority actions |
| **Destructive** | Secondary or text-button geometry, `ink` label + `clay` icon/mark. Use a `clay` state stroke only when extra warning is necessary. Confirmation is required before a destructive action |
| **Text button** | body-strong `ink`, no container; min height 44 |
| **Icon button** | Glyph 20 pt `ink`, 44×44 touch target, no container unless floating (then circle, `paper-raised` fill, `shadow-float`; add a quiet edge only if the background requires it) |
| **Auth buttons** | Height 50, primary recipe |

Present one visually dominant primary action at a time. Never use an accent-filled button.

### 5.2 Cards

**Default card language:** `paper` or `mist-40` fill · radius `md` · padding `lg` · no border. On a `paper` background, use `mist-40` or `shadow-card` when a visible card boundary is necessary. If neither is needed, omit the card container and let spacing establish the group.

- Pattern cards: one shared outer surface with a left icon slot (max 80 pt wide) + main slot, 12 gap; min height 80. Separate the slots with whitespace or a `mist-40` fill, not nested outlines.
- Feed cards: full-width and borderless, with title `heading`, body `body`, metadata `meta` in `ink-60`, and avatar name body-strong Medium. A quiet shadow may be used when needed.
- Quiet variant (dense lists, settings groups): no outline and no shadow. Use section spacing, a tonal group background, or a 1 pt `mist` divider where separation is necessary.
- Do not turn content into a card when a heading, spacing, or simple row grouping communicates the hierarchy more clearly.
- Status on a card = one 8 pt accent dot or icon paired with an `ink` caption — never a fully tinted card background (exception: a 20% accent banner strip inside the card).

### 5.3 Inputs

- Text field: `mist-40` fill, no resting outline, radius `md`, padding 16 h / 14 v, text `body` (sign-up: 22), placeholder `ink-40`. If a field sits on a tonal background, it may use `paper` plus a 1 pt `mist` edge. Focus: add a 2 pt `ink` ring without changing layout; on web use a 2 px outline-offset ring.
- Inline/quiet field (search, in-card): `mist-40` fill, no outline, radius `sm`.
- Error: helper `caption` in `ink` below the field, paired with a `clay` icon or mark. Add a 2 pt `clay` state outline only when the error needs stronger emphasis. Never red-fill.
- Toggles: iOS switch tinted `ink`. Radio/selection: circle icon `ink` when selected, `ink-40` when not, label `body`; row min height 44.
- Selection chips (archetype circles etc.): selected = `ink` fill + `paper` glyph, no outer border, slight lift; unselected = flat `mist-40` fill with no border. A 1 pt `mist` edge is allowed only when the chip disappears into its background.

### 5.4 Chips & pills

`mist-40` fill (pressed: `mist`), no border, radius `md`, padding 12/8, title body-strong + detail `caption` in `ink-60`. Selected chip: `ink` fill with `paper` text, or a checkmark when a dark fill would be too prominent. Use a 1 pt `mist` edge only when needed against the surrounding background. Never accent-fill chips.

### 5.5 Navigation

- **Tab bar:** `paper` background. Add a top hairline `mist` only when content scrolls into the bar and separation is unclear. Active tab: `ink` glyph + `caption` label; inactive: `ink-40`. No accent and no custom pill highlight on iOS26 native bars.
- **Nav bar:** `paper`, title `title` (24) or inline `heading`, back = left-arrow icon button. No large-title system font — Jost only.

### 5.6 Chat (Groups & Arete)

- User bubble: `ink` fill, `paper` text, radius `md` (one bottom-trailing corner `sm`). User may retint via the Arete color setting; default `ink`.
- Other-member bubble: `mist-40` fill, `ink` text, mirrored corner.
- **Arete** (AI): `paper` or `mist-40` bubble with no outline, plus a `fjord` 8 pt identity dot and name in `ink`. Fjord is Arete's reserved identity color everywhere, but the dot should carry the color rather than framing every message.
- System/completion cards in chat: quiet card variant with a `sage` check.
- Prompt chips: per §5.4. Aim for a consistent width around 154 where space permits, but adapt to compact widths and Dynamic Type without clipping.

### 5.7 Badges & progress

- Numeric badges: `ink` circle, `paper` caption numerals. Status dots: 8 pt accent circles.
- Milestone badges (progress sphere): matte `paper` slabs with `ink` engraving; current = `paper-raised`, sharper engraving, slight lift, and one `sage` accent stripe; completed = engraved `sage` check, 100% solid; locked = `ink-40` line work, still solid — never ghost-transparent. Do not turn the current badge into a large black slab.
- Levels use numbers without philosophical stage names: "Level 3" everywhere a level is titled. A level's name is the archetype's region there ("Victorian River"), used as a subtitle (the level-up panel) or as the name in prose (Arete); badge names name badges, never levels. Keep the globe header compact: milestone name on the first line, then the user’s actual level and points to the next level on one row (for example, “Level 1 · 300 pts to Level 2”). Tapping the progress row opens Points; tapping the milestone opens its requirements. Keep practice explanations, detailed totals, and status summaries in the sheet. Do not float a separate points pill over the environment. Provide a return-to-position control while browsing.
- Every milestone connects its symbol to a concrete practice. State that badge tiers are optional and points advance the level; selecting a milestone opens its requirements.
- All 15 milestone symbols use a shared mineral-pigment palette: slate blue `#7E9DB1`, weathered sage `#8D9E86`, dusty terracotta `#B78D80`, muted ochre `#C3B28E`, and smoky mauve `#A399AD`. These fixed artwork colors retain their family identity in dark mode; do not invert desaturated pigments as neutral surfaces. Use the same matte, nonmetallic finish and paper slabs throughout, with a matching low base under every block. The first three detail cards use symbol-only artwork with native text and separate earned-tier stars. Preserve the authored model meshes and Agora clearance when applying presentation changes.
- Bars/rings: track 2 pt `mist`, fill 2 pt (bars 4 pt) `ink`; use `sage` only for "complete".
- Progress sphere: use an opaque porcelain-white shell with a soft ambient shading floor so the surface stays light while retaining curvature. Keep the far-side grid and route occluded. Use a pale geographic graticule that softens toward
  the horizon. Path uses smooth, constant-width connected semicircles with contact shadows and
  stays within the central 90% of screen width.
- Progress camera: Overview uses the higher authored rail with a modest downward tilt to expose upcoming bends and landmarks. Close retains the guided walking perspective. Both follow the path tangent with no free orbit or abrupt lateral swings.
- Sky artwork should give the globe depth and keep space around the sculptures. Dawn Mist uses a cool blue upper sky, warm ivory horizon, and tapered clouds; Night Sky uses ink-blue depth and varied stars; Aurora Ridge uses restrained sage and teal curtains. Their light gently colors the 3D scene and stays aligned with the visible sky while browsing. Cloud drift and scroll parallax are subtle, pause when the app is inactive, and stop with Reduce Motion. Keep ordinary UI colors semantic and independent of the sky palette.
- Progress marker: the authored sculpted triangle, at 60% of its original width and length, with shallow 3D relief and a muted slate-blue finish. It follows the road's tangent. A matching slate-blue fill colors the full inner road surface up to the triangle, leaving both rails neutral. Its endpoint follows the authored road centerline so it meets the triangle without a visible gap. Use #6C8795 in light appearance and #94ABB7 in dark appearance for both wayfinding elements. Solid matte insets with a 0.018 scene-unit radius follow equal arc-length intervals along the road ahead, with a darker neutral tone for visibility on the light road. They are distance cues, not point or badge checkpoints. Travelled marks disappear into the continuous road fill. No hollow rings or cross-road boundary bars. Fade the geographic graticule behind this information.
- Milestone placement: one badge at midpoint/apex of each bend, rooted to local surface normal
  and subtly faced toward camera. Current badge is sharpest; completed stays solid but quieter;
  locked stays legible rather than ghost-transparent.
- Depth: path and badges occlude graticule, objects behind horizon disappear, distant objects
  soften, and badge/path contact shadows establish physical attachment.
- Spider chart, graphs: `ink` lines on `mist` grid; single `sage` data fill at 20%.

### 5.8 Empty states, loading, errors

- Empty state: line-drawn glyph (2 pt ink strokes, ≤ 120 pt), `heading` one-liner, `body` in `ink-60`, optional secondary button. Centered, top-biased (⅓ down). No illustrations with color fills.
- Loading: `ink` spinner or 2 pt indeterminate bar; skeletons `mist-40` blocks with 0.8 s ease-in-out pulse.
- Error banner: `mist-40` or 20% `clay` fill, `clay` icon or short leading rule, and `body` text in `ink`. Use a full 2 pt `clay` state stroke only for an error requiring immediate blocking attention. Toast/confirmation: `ink` pill, `paper` text, bottom, auto-dismiss 2.5 s.

### 5.9 Widgets & Watch

- Widgets: `paper` background with no app-drawn outer border, same type tokens at −2 pt, one accent max. Let the widget host establish its outer boundary.
- Watch: black system background; use `paper` cards sparingly; text `ink`(dark) = `#F2F0ED`; accents identical. Prefer borderless grouping and adjust illustration/control strokes for legibility on each case size.

---

## 6. Motion

Calm and consistent. Use these curves for custom Paths interactions:

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `motion-tap` | easeOut 0.15 s | Press feedback, selection toggles, chip taps |
| `motion-move` | spring(response 0.3, damping 0.82) | Element position/size changes and reordering |
| `motion-fade` | easeOut 0.25 s | Opacity in/out, staged reveals (LevelUp card stagger: 0.25 s steps) |
| `motion-scene` | easeInOut 0.35 s | Custom scene transitions and camera reframes |
| `motion-ambient` | easeInOut 1.5–2.5 s repeatForever | Background/breathing effects only |

Rules: no bouncy springs for ordinary UI; nothing decorative animates on loop in content areas; respect Reduce Motion (drop ambient + replace moves with fades); progress-sphere camera follows the guided-walk rules in §5.7. Keep platform-owned navigation and presentation transitions native unless a custom transition has a clear product purpose. Specialized visualizations may tune timing while preserving the same calm character.

---

## 7. Iconography

- Source: SF Symbols (weight **medium**, matching Jost's optical weight) or project `SVGAssets` drawn at 2 pt stroke on 24 pt grid.
- Sizes: 16 (inline), 20 (standard/buttons), 24 (tab bar, list leads), 30 (card icon slot).
- Color: `ink` / `ink-40` (disabled) / `paper` (on ink fills); accent tint only when the icon itself is the status mark.
- Never mix filled and outline variants of the same symbol across screens — Paths uses **outline** variants by default; filled only for active tab and selection states.

---

## 8. Voice & tone

- **Calm coach, not cheerleader.** "Pattern complete." not "Awesome job!! 🎉"
- Sentence case everywhere, including buttons ("Schedule pattern"). Exceptions: `overline` labels are uppercase.
- No exclamation marks, no emoji in UI chrome (emoji allowed only inside user content).
- Verbs first on buttons: "Start session", "Join group", "Keep streak".
- Errors state the fix, not the fault: "Add a name to continue."
- Numbers over adjectives: "3-day streak" not "great streak".
- Arete speaks in the same voice — measured, second person, ≤ 2 sentences per prompt.

---

## 9. Enforcement (for the LLM writing code)

1. **Forbidden in ordinary feature UI:** `Color(hex:)` and `.fromStoredHex` outside token/user-color files; hard-coded visible text styles instead of `PathsFont`; new `ButtonStyle`s duplicating §5.1; and `ultraThinMaterial` on ordinary content cards. Specialized rendering, debug views, platform-owned controls, and documented optical corrections are allowed exceptions.
2. Tokens live in `Paths/Styles/DesignSystem.swift` + `Colors.swift` (iOS) and one `tokens.css` (web). When a genuinely recurring value needs a new token, update this guide alongside the implementation.
3. Style chain used 2+ times → extract to ViewModifier/ButtonStyle/component.
4. Do not add a border during migration merely to make an existing component match a shared recipe. Add one only when it represents focus, selection, error, or a boundary that is unclear without it.
5. Every new screen ships passing the checklist: semantic type tokens · role tokens · shared spacing/radius where applicable · shared button/input variants · no unnecessary borders or nested containers · ≤ 1 accent per component · 44 pt touch targets · light + dark verified · keyboard + Dynamic Type verified · iPhone + iPad widths verified.
6. Migration order (from `docs/final-steps/product/DESIGN_CONSISTENCY_CONTRACT.md`): Groups/Social → Calendar/Progress/Profile → Methods/legacy. Zero new drift from today.

---

*End of guide. Anything not specified here defaults to the nearest rule above. If genuinely unspecified, choose the quieter option with fewer containers, fewer effects, and no new border.*
